newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China tells Philippines to release fishermen.
newsitem.headline: China tells Philippines to release fishermen.

text.p: China pressed the Philippines on Thursday to release 21 Chinese fishermen held since last month for entering an area of the South China Sea both countries claim.
"We hope the Philippine side would unconditionally release the 21 Chinese fishermen and their vessel at an early date," the Chinese embassy said in a statement.

The Philippines arrested the men on May 20 after catching them fishing near the Scarborough Shoal, a barely visible outcrop of rocks within its 200-mile exclusive economic zone but which Beijing insists belong historically to China.
The arrests have added to the increasing tension between the two over who owns some of the tiny islands and reefs in the South China Sea, some of them believed to have rich deposits of oil and gas.
The Scarborough Shoal lies north of the Spratly Islands, claimed either in part or in whole by China, the Philippines and four other Asian countries.
On Wednesday, the Philippines appeared to soften its stand on the fishermen with a committee recommending charges of illegal entry be substituted for illegal fishing.
"I have taken note of the report. The 21 Chinese fishermen were conducting normal fishing activity in the Chinese water," the embassy statement said.
The issue has created furious reaction in the Philippines with some accusing the Chinese of near-invasion of a country whose naval might consists of a handful of 40- year-old ships.
Some analysts have suggested fears have been deliberately fanned by the military as it tries to squeeze more funds out of Congress to build up its weaponry.
Others contend Beijing is testing the resolve among Southeast Asian nations to look after each other by putting pressure on its weakest member.

Philippine officials say that under the United Nations Convention on Law of the Sea, foreign vessels can pass through a country's exclusive economic zone provided they do not exploit resources in the area.
But the Philippine Navy found tonnes of fish on the Chinese boat.
